title: A carried puck stays with its carrier through a body's touch: it is taken with a key or not at all
pillar: P1 the puck is yours until someone takes it with a key
hypothesis: The cause was confirmed both ways in the gym before this ran (rinklab probe -which=take; ROUND-2.md). Round 1's guess (the bodies' bounce throws the carrier's velocity) was wrong: the puck changes hands one or two frames BEFORE the bodies touch. The attacker's body meets the puck on the carrier's blade; thirdjam's BlockCarried pushes it out of that body and takes out its motion into him; the puck then moves at the closing speed against its own carrier, RidingCarrier's 4 m/s test calls it loose, and the human's ring (R-0069) or a bot's pickup arc takes it on that frame: head on 12 of 12 scenes without a key for human on bot and bot on bot, 0 of 4 for a bot on the human (his own ring takes it back). So the leak is one-sided: the human takes pucks by skating into carriers, the opposing bots take them from his mates the same way, and nobody takes them from him. With the switch the puck keeps its carrier's velocity through another body's touch and through his own bounce: 0 of 12. Expected in matches: the human's takes with no key near 0 (T5: 4.4 a minute for the planning hand); a hand that only skates falls toward the idle hand (PLAY: 29.5 % against 9.5 %); the poke, the lift and the body check become the way to win a puck, so taking each away now costs (T7); the mates keep the puck longer against opposing bodies, so possession and passes received may rise; the human's own carry does not get longer by this (he already kept his). Risk: the hands lose their cheapest way to win the puck and the ladder falls.
tempo: none: no row of the tempo map moves (the gym probes are equal); the probe 'commit, none, head' (a take with no key, 20 of 21) goes to 0

why: The rule does what the owner ruled in thirdjam (R-0048) and thirdjam leaked. Gym: a take with no key head on, 12 of 12 before, 0 of 12 after, for the human on a bot and bot on bot. In matches (60 seeds, paired): the mates keep the pucks the human gives them, so the planning hand's passes that reach a mate rise from 56.7 to 67.3 % at pro (T3's first half met for that hand: 65 %), 54.8 to 61.5 % at all-star; it is knocked down less (4.5 to 3.7 a match, 9.3 to 7.3 s on the ice); possession changes 28.0 to 26.8 a minute. The stick lift became a verb that matters: without it the planning hand loses 10 points (81.7 to 71.7; before the rule 85 to 81.7). The price is the cheap take: the planning novice at pro falls 65 to 43.3 % (-21.7 +-8.6), the regular 85 to 81.7 (-3.3 +-6.7), the good 93.3 to 96.7; all-star regular 66.7 to 55 (-11.7 +-9.2, inside two standard errors); thirdjam's scripted regular hand 63.3 to 53.3 at pro (-10 +-8.5). The spread at pro (43 / 82 / 97) is wider, not narrower, so T8 is not broken; the level table (round 3) sets where it sits. Two things it showed and did not cure: the body check now costs the planning hand (90 % without it against 81.7 %, +8.3; paired against its own before +11.7 +-5.9), and the poke is still worth nothing (86.7 % without it).
owner_line: Skating into a man who has the puck no longer gives it to you: you bounce off him and he still has it. Press the stick lift (or poke, or hit him) and it is yours. Your mates stop losing the puck to a bump the moment you pass to them.
notes: The "takes key / no key" column is a loose count (any time the human carries within 20 frames of an opponent carrying: it includes passes he cut and pucks a mate knocked loose), so it falls (4.26 to 2.81 a minute) but not to 0. The strict count (the puck rode with an opponent at the end of one frame and is the human's at the end of the next, no key of his in the 30 frames before) was added to the observer after this ran: see the round notes for its figure on both arms. READ WITH CARE (added after the mid-round matrix): this experiment was read through the planning hand before its press timing was repaired (epoch k8-2). Its statements about single verbs (the lift worth 10 points, the body check costing its user) did not survive the repaired hand (ROUND-2.md section 5: the lift +11.7 +-5.9 without it, the check +1.7) and are not findings. What stands: the gym (12 of 12 to 0 of 12), the strict take count in matches (1.23 to 0.33 a minute on that hand; 0.60 to 0.27 on the repaired one), the passes that reach a mate, and the direction of the ladder's move.
